text: Hide behind a pillar and your health comes back. Reach a sentry from behind and you can pick it up, or simply walk into it. It falls over. Gently. Mostly.
The ceiling over the first sentry takes portals, and so does the floor beside your crate. After that, a broken sentry makes a very good umbrella.
You dropped a box on one sentry and hid behind its body from the others. I am not sure which of us should be more ashamed.
Testing was complete. Then I found some more tests. You are welcome.
This door wants two weights. I have provided one crate and one sentry. The sentry does not know it is a weight yet.
A sentry sleeps while you carry it, and wakes a moment after you put it down. Think about which way it will be facing when it does. It certainly will.
You used a guard as a paperweight. Its supervisor would be furious, if it still had one.
The corridor ahead is watched. Eighteen metres of it. I counted, and so will the sentry at the far end.
There is a second sentry in this room, facing the wall. It is in disgrace. You may borrow it.
Sentries do not shoot at what they cannot see. Hold something large between you and the one at the end. Something roughly sentry shaped.
It never saw you. It will file a report saying a colleague walked up to it and left. Nobody will read it. Nobody reads any of them.
Two sentries, one lane each, and a wall in the middle for you to cower behind. I had the wall put in specially.
They were never told about portals. It was a budget decision.
Each sentry is staring at a white pillar. If its pillar showed it the other sentry, the two of them would have a short and productive disagreement. The door wants a weight afterwards.
They shot each other. I would report it, but that department was closed. Most of them were.
The crate is in a pen. The pen has no door. I designed it that way, and then I lost the drawings.
The purple panel reverses gravity inside the pen. For crates. Not for you. You stay where I can see you.
Things that fall up will fall into a portal on the ceiling as happily as into one on the floor. Decide where the crate comes out before you step on the panel.
The crate fell up, then sideways, then down. It has now seen more of this facility than you have. Let us keep it that way.
The plate with the amber ring is on a relay. It holds the door for three seconds after you step off it. Three. I was feeling generous.
The door is across the acid. You will need to be quick, which is not a word that appears in your file.
Leave one portal beside the timed plate and the other beside the door before you start. And the door wants the crate as well, on the plate over there.
Three seconds, and you had nearly half of one to spare. Do not look so pleased. The offices are empty. Nobody saw.
That channel is coolant. It keeps me at a comfortable temperature, and you at a fatal one. Things float in it. You are not one of the things.
The door over there wants a weight. The field across the floor recycles anything you carry. I do enjoy it when the rules agree with each other.
The float in the channel will carry whatever stands on it, once the pump is running. The amber plate runs the pump. Mind which way your passenger is looking when it arrives.
You sent a sentry on a cruise. It is the only holiday anyone here has had in a very long time. Including me. Especially me.
A gravity panel. It turns down into up for everything in that zone that is not bolted down, or you. You are exempt. Legal insisted.
Please do not shoot the observation offices. Nobody is in them. Nobody has been in them for some time.
A live sentry jams portals near it. I did not want them wandering off.
You are carrying a sentry. It weighs forty kilograms and has no sense of humour. You have a lot in common.
Put me down!
I can walk. I choose not to.
Friendly fire! Friendly fire!
I thought we were colleagues!
Was it something I said?
Et tu, unit seven?
Timber.
I meant to do that.
The floor is closer than it looks.
